lead: B. R. Ambedkar was an economist, born on 14 April 1891 in Bhim Janmabhoomi and Dr. Ambedkar Nagar.
He died on 6 December 1956 in Dr. Ambedkar National Memorial at the age of 65.

He is associated with work such as Annihilation of Caste, Castes in India: Their Mechanism, Genesis and Development and Who Were the Shudras? and has held the office of member of Rajya Sabha and Minister of Law and Justice of India.
This profile collects the B. facts readers search for most — date of birth and current age, height and physical stats, family and relationship details, education, and a dated career timeline.

sections.heading: B. R. Ambedkar — Early Life, Family and Education
paras: B. R. Ambedkar was born on 14 April 1891 in Bhim Janmabhoomi and Dr. Ambedkar Nagar, and holds citizenship of British Raj and India. He was given the name Bhīvā Rāmjī Sakpāḷ at birth and is publicly known as B. R. Ambedkar.
Public records name his father, Ramji Maloji Sakpal and his mother, Bhimabai Ramji Sakpal.
He received his education at Columbia University, London School of Economics and Political Science and Elphinstone College.
He is recorded as speaking English, German, Pali and Sanskrit.

sections.heading: B. R. Ambedkar — Career and Professional Work
paras: B. R. Ambedkar works primarily as an economist, politician, constitutionalist, barrister, jurist and sociologist.

Among the credits most often linked to B. are Annihilation of Caste, Castes in India: Their Mechanism, Genesis and Development, Who Were the Shudras?, The Buddha and His Dhamma, Waiting for a Visa, Small Holdings in India and Their Remedies, The Problem of the Rupees: Its Origin and Its Solution, The Evolution of Provincial Finance in British India, Pakistan or Partition of India and Ranade, Gandhi and Jinnah.

He has held the following offices: member of Rajya Sabha (1952–1956), Minister of Law and Justice of India (1947–1951), chairperson (1946–1950), Member of the Constituent Assembly of India (1946–1950), Member of the Advisory Committee of the Constituent Assembly of India (1947–1950) and minister of labor (1942–1946). He is affiliated with Scheduled Castes Federation.
He has taken part in British-Indian Round Table Conferences.

He is a parent to Yashwant Ambedkar.
